fixed.summary: A GPU pass's time is now its time alone on the GPU. Its beginning to its end included its waits: Metal samples a pass's beginning as its encoder starts, so on an M4 Pro a 90.7 ms frame's small post passes read about 20 ms each, 413 ms in all. gpuPasses and the gpu thread now give each pass's stretches with nothing else in flight; the gpu frame's args give each pass's alone (`passes`) and in-flight (`inFlight`) milliseconds and the frame's `overlapped` and `idle`, which with the alone time sum to its span. In-flight spans are named `<pass> (in flight)` on the `gpu in flight N` threads.

added.summary: `og cost . --off "<og run options>"` measures what a feature costs the real frame: at least 4 traced runs a side, on and off alternating, each side's median GPU frame span with its range and the machine's load, and their difference (render guide §10).
`og run --gpu-serial` makes every render-graph pass wait for the one before it, so a pass's alone time in the trace is its cost in isolation. Not in a publish build.
